Reporting directly to our CTO, you’ll collaborate with a small, high-impact team to deliver user experiences across Dividend.com, MutualFunds.com and other brands within our portfolio. This role combines expert Ruby on Rails skills with AI integration expertise, requiring you to leverage LLMs in your development workflow, state management and user interactions. You’ll work in a remote-first hybrid environment, which encourages in person collaboration, using ShapeUp to manage projects that trade-off on-time delivery for de-scoped outcomes. As a technical leader, you'll have a seat at the table shaping system architecture, implementing core features all while embracing an entrepreneurial mindset and a “get things done” mentality. Responsibilities Architect and maintain Rails applications (Rails 8) Integrate LLMs into our microservices architecture for state management and real-time user experiences. Enhance front-end experiences with Hotwire, StimulusJS, or React, ensuring seamless AI-driven interactions. Optimize LLM inference for low latency and cost, using caching and asynchronous processing. Required Technical Skills Back-End Ruby (5+ years, expert-level) Ruby on Rails (Rails 6-8 preferred) PostgreSQL (or MySQL) Elasticsearch Redis Docker Front-End StimulusJS or JavaScript ES6 Tailwind CSS HTML HTTP AI Integration Experience integrating AI/ML models (e.g., LLMs, NLP) with web applications Familiarity with LLM frameworks (e.g., LangChain, Hugging Face) or APIs (e.g., xAI, Anthropic) Nice-to-Have Technical Skills Kubernetes for microservices orchestration React for advanced front-end components Graph databases for complex financial data Contributions to open-source RoR or AI projects Required Soft Skills Entrepreneurial mindset with a passion for AI and FinTech Natural leader who mentors and inspires teammates Problem-solver with a “get things done” mentality Excellent communication, thriving in remote and cross-team collaboration Attention to detail, ensuring clean, maintainable code Team player comfortable as an individual contributor Why Join Us? Impactful Work : Build AI-powered tools that help millions of investors make informed decisions from data-driven insights. Cutting-Edge Tech : Work with Rails 8, LLMs, and modern tools like Hotwire, Databricks, and xAI’s API in a microservices architecture. Autonomy and Influence : Collaborate directly with our CEO and CTO to shape our AI-driven platform, with freedom to innovate. Competitive Compensation : $160,000–$200,000 CAD/USD (based on experience) and benefits. Remote Flexibility : Remote-first (±3 hours from ET) with hybrid in office collaboration in Toronto or NYC Growth Opportunities : Budget for AI and Rails conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, RailsConf), plus access to cutting-edge AI tools for experimentation. Dynamic Culture : Join a small, no-ego team passionate about trust, innovation, and making a difference in FinTech. About Mitre Media’s AI-Driven Platform Mitre Media powers premium financial brands like Dividend.com and MutualFunds.com with the Mitre Platform. This platform integrates traditional content management, financial data, first-party data, ad revenue, and subscription tools, all enhanced by LLMs for rich, user-focused experiences. Our data-derived insights delight users, while our advertising solutions deliver unmatched performance for partners like BlackRock and Vanguard, leveraging advanced targeting and first-party data. How to Apply Submit your resume, GitHub profile, and a brief note on why you’re excited about building AI-driven FinTech to jobs@mitremedia.com.

title: Face Deduplication Collection
description: The project compensation rate is $0.55 USD per accepted image. The objective of this project is to collect a large and diverse dataset of current neutral selfies, head-pose captures, and historical facial images to support machine-learning research and facial recognition model training at TELUS. The focus is on capturing real-world variation across lighting, poses, expressions, accessories, environments, and aging to improve model accuracy and robustness. The collection includes: • Current Neutral Selfies – clean frontal selfies serving as high-quality identity references, with natural variation in appearance and surroundings. • Current Head-Pose Captures – selfies captured in assigned head directions to introduce pose variation. • Historical Images – older photos from participants’ galleries to capture natural aging and long-term appearance changes. To qualify for payment, you must submit a minimum of 20 valid images. The maximum payout is based on 24 accepted images. Due to the strict automated and manual Quality Control (QC) process, we strongly recommend submitting 30 images to help ensure that enough images remain valid after review Note: Please use a Gmail address as your primary account when applying for this project. description: Job Description The Surveyor I is an entry or junior-level position for new graduates and/or those candidates with less than five (5) years of experience in an applicable industry. The Surveyor I, under a direct supervisor, performs work involving conventional surveying practices. The primary function is to develop the ability to effectively examine and report on vessels and other marine structures during and after construction relative to compliance with the applicable requirements for maintaining the vessel in Classification with ABS and meeting associated statutory and special service requirements related to Safety of Life at Sea, Loadline, Tonnage, Cargo Gear and Pollution Prevention Certification. What You Will Do (with the assistance and guidance of an experienced ABS Surveyor): Acts as a professional specialist for the organization in the application of related rules, regulations, requirements, concepts, principles, and processes. Performs routine surveys on classed vessels, platforms, or other marine structures and at manufacturers for classification and compliance with statutory requirements. Prepares technically accurate and timely reports of inspections and surveys performed. Engages in contact with clients to resolve problems within areas of expertise. Maintains survey files in an orderly and up-to-date manner in the area of responsibility. Develops the skills necessary for the administration of office procedures and monitoring of business performance at an assigned port. Through broader and more technically challenging work assignments, the individual must develop a thorough understanding of field operations, policies, methods, and procedures. What You Will Need: Education and Experience Qualifications from a tertiary institution within a relevant field of engineering or physical science (minimum two (2) years program); or Qualifications from a marine or nautical institution and relevant seagoing experience as a certificated ship officer, and Proficiency in the English language commensurate with the scope of statutory certification and services and, before assignment, with their future work. Appropriate certification and/or licenses in areas of specialization may be required. Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities Ability to develop a working knowledge of ABS Rules, Guides, statutory regulations, and related instructions, as well as the ABS Employee Safety Policy. Ability to read engineering plans and have a basic understanding of shipbuilding practices and vessel operations. Ability to perform surveys in the prescribed format. Knowledge of computer programs or software packages related to job responsibilities. Knowledge of related technical interfaces required for group project work. Knowledge of ships' engineering systems and machinery. Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, pertinent information relative to assigned area of technical expertise. Ability to analyze problems and propose solutions. Responsiveness to customers and the ability to work well with others. Ability to become familiar with the ABS Health, Safety, Quality, and Environmental Management Systems. Physical Requirements: Where allowed by local laws, a pre-employment physical examination is mandatory. The role of surveyor/auditor requires sufficient physical strength, stamina, agility, and both visual and auditory acuity to perform the listed duties effectively. The ability to climb vertical ladders up to nine meters and navigate steep steps is essential. Shall be capable of working at heights on various staging and lifting equipment. Shall be able to maneuver in tight spaces and work inside confined areas for extended periods, including kneeling and crawling. The role may involve exposure to industrial environments, potential injury risks, extreme weather conditions, and demanding physical activities. Shall be able to lift at least 25 lbs. / 11.34 kgs. title: Mercury: Counsel, Product & Regulatory - Payments & AML
description: Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States In 1905, chief engineer John Stevens inherited one of the most ambitious infrastructure projects in history: the Panama Canal. The challenge wasn’t digging a ditch between two oceans. It was figuring out how to move ships safely through a system of locks, gates, reservoirs, and changing conditions without bringing global commerce to a halt. The solution wasn’t to stop movement. It was to create a framework that allowed movement at scale. Modern financial infrastructure presents a similar challenge. Payment systems, banking products, compliance obligations, and regulatory frameworks all exist for a reason. The goal isn’t to eliminate complexity. It’s to build systems that allow innovation, growth, and customer value within it. Who we are Since 2019, Mercury has been on a mission to reinvent banking‡ for the modern age. We blend elegant design and cutting-edge technology to offer checking and savings accounts, debit cards, payment services, credit products, cash management tools, and sophisticated analytics. Everything we build reflects our belief that financial products should be thoughtfully crafted, fast, transparent, and genuinely enjoyable to use. As we continue expanding and iterating on our product offerings and as we work to build a nationally chartered bank, we’re looking for a Counsel, Product & Regulatory (Payments & AML) to help us navigate increasingly complex questions at the intersection of product, regulation, and financial infrastructure. About the team Our Product & Regulatory Legal team operates like the rest of Mercury: with urgency, curiosity, and a bias toward action. We embed with product teams from early ideation through launch, working alongside engineers, designers, compliance partners, operations teams, and risk stakeholders to get products right. We move fast, we take ownership, and we don’t wait to be asked. If something needs figuring out, we’re up to the task. We are not a team that sits on the sidelines reviewing finished proposals. We work alongside our partners to identify risks, unlock opportunities, and find practical paths forward. We care deeply about good judgment, strong relationships, and building frameworks that scale. What you’ll do Advise on payments products and infrastructure. You’ll support a broad portfolio of payments-related initiatives across Mercury. You’ll advise on matters involving payment rails, product launches, operational incidents, partner relationships, and customer-facing experiences. You’ll help product teams navigate regulatory complexity while continuing to build exceptional products. Partner across the company. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Compliance, Risk, Engineering, Operations, Partnerships, and Legal. You’ll build trusted relationships across these functions and bring legal perspective into conversations early, not as a checkpoint, but as a low-ego, high-ownership thought partner. Help launch new capabilities. Mercury is continuing to expand its product offerings while building a nationally chartered bank. You’ll support new payment capabilities (like Zelle) from early exploration through launch, helping teams identify risks, evaluate options, and make sound decisions in ambiguous environments. Support financial crimes initiatives. You’ll work closely with Mercury’s AML Advisory, Sanctions, Compliance, and Risk teams on matters involving financial crimes compliance. You’ll help interpret requirements, evaluate new initiatives, and develop practical guidance that enables teams to move efficiently while maintaining an appropriate risk posture. Build scalable guidance. The best legal advice solves more than the question in front of you. You’ll help create frameworks and guidance that improve consistency, reduce friction, and allow the organization to make better decisions over time. Use AI intentionally. Bring a working knowledge of AI tools in legal workflows and a genuine interest in finding new ways to drive efficiency. We’re building a legal team that works smarter, not just harder. Stay curious and adaptable. The regulatory and product landscape continues to evolve quickly. New payment rails emerge. Regulatory expectations shift. Business priorities change. You’ll embrace that complexity and continue learning alongside it. What you should have 4+ years of legal experience. Active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction. Experience supporting fintechs, banks, payment companies, sponsor-bank programs, payment networks, BaaS providers, or regulators with substantial payments- or AML-related exposure. Strong working knowledge of payments-related regulatory frameworks, and an interest in emerging areas like stablecoins. Familiarity with BSA/AML and sanctions requirements. Exceptional communication skills. You know your audience and tailor accordingly. Strong judgment and comfort operating in ambiguous environments. A proactive sense of ownership. You’re comfortable saying, “I don’t know yet, but I’ll find out.” Genuine curiosity about financial products, financial infrastructure, and the evolving regulatory landscape. Strong working knowledge of AI use cases within legal roles and/or financial services generally and genuine interest in using AI to drive efficiency in your work. What will make you successful here Mercury is a place where lawyers are expected to have a point of view. Not just about what a regulation requires, but about how a product can meet that requirement in a way that’s thoughtful, scalable, and good for customers. The people who thrive on this team treat ambiguity as an invitation rather than a reason to pause. They read a regulation and think about what it permits, not just what it prohibits. They understand that legal advice is most valuable when it helps the business make a decision, not when it simply identifies a risk. You’ll also spend a meaningful amount of your time on work that may not look like traditional legal practice: helping scope cross-functional projects, pressure-testing product designs, navigating operational questions, and building processes alongside compliance and operational partners. If you’re energized by that kind of work, and if you measure your impact by whether the product, process, or customer experience got better—not just whether the memo was technically correct—you’ll do well here. Why this role This is an opportunity to join Mercury during a uniquely consequential period of growth. You’ll help support existing products while contributing to the development of new capabilities as Mercury builds a nationally chartered bank. You’ll work alongside experienced legal, compliance, product, and banking professionals, gain exposure to a wide range of regulatory and product questions, and have meaningful ownership early in your career. You’ll also help shape how Mercury approaches payments and financial crimes legal support for years to come. The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options), and benefits. Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers. Our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following: US employees in New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $186,400 - $209,700 US employees outside of the New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $167,800 - $188,700 Canadian employees (any location): $176,100 - $198,200 CAD While we’ve received conditional approval to become a bank, Mercury today is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. description: About the role The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. About Arabian Private Holdings Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations. Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies. Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals. Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates. Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews. title: Toggl: Events & Field Marketing Manager
description: Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/ We are looking for an Events & Field Marketing Manager to own Toggl's presence made physical, the person who turns a conference badge, a booth conversation, or a dinner reservation into real business. The salary for this position is €70,000 annually , and we are committed to reviewing salaries every year based on company and individual performance. You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-5 and UTC+2. This role runs events on both sides of the Atlantic, so you'll need to be able to travel to both North America and Europe. Overview We believe, now more than ever, that in-person moments cut through marketing noise in a way nothing digital can: a handshake, a shared meal, a five-minute conversation where someone finally "gets it." This role is responsible for engineering those moments on purpose, again and again, and ensuring they don't evaporate the second the event ends. You are someone who has done this before (preferably in a B2B SaaS setting) and can negotiate a vendor contract in the morning, rewrite an invitation email by lunch, and walk a trade show floor in the afternoon, reading which conversations are worth a follow-up call. The role As Events & Field Marketing Manager, you own the full lifecycle of Toggl's in-person and hybrid presence, turning sponsorships, trade shows, and owned experiences into a genuine pipeline engine, not just a brand awareness play. Your main responsibilities will be: Sponsored event execution: Take full, end-to-end operational coordination ownership for all major external sponsorships and industry trade shows. You'll manage vendor communications, booth layout architecture, graphic dimension configurations, compliance logistics, and swag sourcing & distribution, owning the event budget and negotiating with vendors along the way. Event content & communications : Write and produce all content required to run an event end-to-end — invitations, landing pages, promotional emails, social posts, on-site materials, and post-event follow-up sequences. You'll also create post-event recap content (summary emails, LinkedIn posts, short highlight videos, and case studies where relevant) to extend the life of each event well beyond its final day. Pipeline coordination : Eliminate post-event pipeline latency by building strict cross-departmental SLAs before any event takes place. You'll work directly with Sales and our Demand Gen Manager to build pre-event ad layers, account matching lists, and post-event outbound sequencing so event contacts are in active sales conversations within 24 hours. Owned experiential events : Research, conceptualize, and execute curated physical event touchpoints (think micro-roundtables and private VIP executive dinners) specifically designed for upmarket decision-makers, managing everything from venue negotiation and culinary curation to guest list outreach and on-site execution. Other responsibilities include: Owning the event lead capture process and ensuring all attendee data flows cleanly into HubSpot with correct source attribution. Reporting on cost-per-opportunity for each activation to showcase the impact of event and field marketing activities. Collaborating with Marketing and Sales to align event initiatives with overall pipeline and business goals. Using AI tools extensively in your daily work for research, synthesis, analysis, drafting, and exploration. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact. What success looks like Success in this role means every event Toggl touches has a clear plan for turning attendees into pipeline before it even happens. It means vendor logistics and budgets are handled without drama, event content extends the life of each activation for weeks afterward, and no lead ever sits untouched for more than 24 hours. Over time, this role builds a repeatable playbook for events, one where Toggl knows its cost-per-opportunity by activation type and can confidently decide which trade shows, sponsorships, and owned experiences are worth doing again. About you You will thrive in this role if you: Know exactly how to run events that convert , and you've been doing it for at least 3-5 years. You love bringing new ideas to the table and have experience with event logistics, vendor negotiation, and field marketing strategies. Have run in-person B2B events in the North American market. You know the conference circuit there, how sponsorship packages get priced and negotiated, which venues and vendors actually deliver, and what North American buyers expect from a booth conversation. Experience in European markets too is a plus, since roughly half the calendar sits here. Are great with people. The thought of hosting a room full of decision-makers, whether at a trade show booth or an intimate executive dinner, is something that excites you. You know how to make people feel looked after without losing sight of the commercial goal. Are incredibly autonomous (and love it). You have run successful B2B events and sponsorships in the past and know what works, what doesn't, and what metrics you need to track (major bonus points if you've specifically marketed software before). You can effectively convey how you will build a similarly high-performing events motion at Toggl. Are equal parts operator and creative , but most importantly, you are relentless about follow-through. You know an event is only as good as what happens in the 24 hours after it ends, and you build the systems to make sure nothing falls through the cracks. Want to have fun with marketing. You will be proactive in bringing new event formats and ideas to the table, finding opportunities for Toggl to show up in the room where it matters most. Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI for research, analysis, drafting, and prototyping as a core part of how you work, not a side experiment. Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters. Have excellent written communication skills and are as comfortable drafting a sharp event invitation as you are briefing Sales on a post-event handoff plan. Asynchronous communication is something you are happy with, and you can concisely express ideas without having to jump on a call. This Role Is NOT A booth babysitter or a logistics coordinator whose job ends when the stand comes down. A pure brand awareness play where "impressions" and "booth visits" are the headline metric. An order-taker who executes the event list someone else decided on. A role that hands leads to Sales and walks away. A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work. Recruitment Steps Skill Assessment AI-Interview Home assignment Interview with Liz, Head of Marketing Paid Test Week The Team We are a global team of ~100 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results. What's Happening at Toggl Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl Focus. One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. Benefits Freedom to choose when and how much you work—we only measure results 24 days of paid time off a year, plus your local holidays Unlimited sick leave In-person meetups for team-building (expenses covered) 4-6 weeks paid sabbatical (depending on tenure) Laptop budget up to 2,500€ and it renews every 3 years €2,000 budget to set up your home office and an additional €300 every year after 3 years of tenure €3,000 per year for co-working space membership and/or internet service at home €4,000 per year contribution to use for training, workshops, and conferences €2,400 per year contribution for any equipment or services to improve and/or maintain your physical and mental health Support for buying tools you need for doing your best work (even eyeglasses if you need a new pair) To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toggl-events-field-marketing-manager

title: The Humane League: Temporary US Corporate Relations Specialist
description: Headquarters: United States URL: https://thehumaneleague.org/ WHO WE ARE The Humane League (THL) is a global nonprofit ending the abuse of animals raised for food. THL fosters a high-energy culture of teamwork and mission-driven problem solving, and we have earned recognition as Top Charity from Animal Charity Evaluators for all of their rating periods. Over the past few years, we’ve grown to a staff of 100+ talented individuals dispersed around the world. At THL, how animals are treated in the food system is at the forefront of our everyday work. We welcome all mission-aligned candidates to apply, no matter where you are in your journey to end the abuse of animals raised for food. YOUR OPPORTUNITY As the Temporary Corporate Relations Specialist, you will play an important role in supporting The Humane League’s efforts to engage with corporations and advance protections for animals in the food supply chain. You are motivated to make a difference in the lives of animals and have the passion to encourage corporate decision makers to do the same. Your primary goal is to support and conduct outreach to bring issues of animal welfare to key decision makers at food companies and their business affiliates. Through research, data-management, and outreach, you will contribute to building relationships and advancing corporate commitments and policies on animal welfare. You will support outreach efforts that increase the number of companies engaged and contribute to measurable progress against corporate commitments, including organizational goals tied to company policy advancement. In this role, you will work closely with the Sr. Corporate Relations Manager, US to support and lead corporate outreach plans, maintain accurate and up-to-date records of engagement, and share insights with the broader team to inform ongoing work while continuing to develop your knowledge of the food industry and corporate engagement strategies. You are a self-driven communicator who can effectively deliver messages in a professional corporate environment. You are comfortable managing your day-to-day responsibilities independently while seeking guidance on more complex situations and collaborating closely with your team. This role is well-suited for someone who enjoys research, relationship-building, persuasive communication and continuous learning while developing experience in corporate engagement, negotiation support, and advocacy work. This position reports directly to the Sr. Corporate Relations Manager, US. This is a temporary full-time, remote position lasting one-year (12 months) in duration, with the possibility of transitioning to a permanent role at The Humane League’s discretion. This role is based in the United States or Canada. To the extent permitted by law, in order to enable collaboration with other global team members, you may be required to work occasional hours outside of 9am - 5pm, depending on your time zone. This position requires domestic and international travel, equivalent to 2 or more trips per year lasting 2 - 4 nights in duration. We will be recording a webinar hosted by Liz Fergus, Sr. Corporate Relations Manager, US, Aimee Drugan, Sr. US Corporate Relations Lead, and Debbie Malenke, Sr. Corporate Relations Lead. The webinar recording will be available to watch here by August 13th. Please submit your application by Friday, August 21 at 11:59 p.m. EST . We encourage early applications and will continue accepting submissions while the role is posted on our website. After this date, we will begin advancing candidates and may close the posting early or extend the deadline as needed. If you are experiencing technical issues, please contact careers@thehumaneleague.org . Please submit applications and all supporting documents in English. All application questions and materials need to be submitted here through the application submission form; we do not accept applications through our careers email. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES Execute outreach to decision makers at food companies through email, written materials, phone calls, virtual meetings, and occasional in-person engagement. Support communication of proposed animal welfare measures and contribute to ongoing relationship management with corporate contacts to encourage policy adoption and progress toward existing commitments. Participate in meetings and negotiations with corporate representatives, documenting outcomes and tracking progress toward animal welfare commitments while escalating complex issues to the Sr. Corporate Relations Manager, US as appropriate. Conduct research to identify and verify information on food companies, industry trends, and corporate structures, including hard-to-find information, while evaluating source credibility. Maintain and update CRM systems with accurate, timely data on outreach activities, contacts, and company progress, and share relevant industry insights with the broader team to inform engagement efforts. Execute on outreach plans and schedules developed in collaboration with team leadership, managing multiple outreach streams and competing deadlines, and adapting priorities as business needs evolve. Support outreach efforts tied to public reports and broader corporate engagement campaigns. Collaborate with colleagues across teams and coordinate with external coalition partners to support campaign priorities, share research and contribute to coordinated corporate engagement efforts. Develop a working knowledge of the food industry landscape, including key players, corporate decision-making structures, and relevant animal welfare policies and issues. Utilize digital tools and platforms such as Salesforce, Google Workspace, Asana, and other software to manage outreach activities and maintain organized data. Develop proficiency in research, outreach, and internal systems with support from team leadership during the onboarding and ramp period. In addition to the above essential job duties, other duties may be assigned as business needs arise. These may include non-essential, marginal job duties. REQUIRED SKILLS Experience: 2+ years of professional or non-professional experience in corporate relations, the food industry, corporate sustainability, ESG, animal science, communications, economics, farm animal advocacy, law or policy, negotiations, research, sales, or other related fields involving relationship management and persuasive communication. Execution, Ownership, and Problem Solving: Demonstrates the ability to manage assigned work independently with minimal supervision while following established processes. Applies sound judgment to resolve routine challenges, identifies opportunities for improvements, and seeks guidance on more complex issues as needed. Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to confidently represent THL through emails, presentations, phone calls, and meetings with corporate stakeholders. Builds and maintains productive relationships through professionalism, diplomacy, active listening, and persuasive communication. Resilience and Adaptability: Comfortable engaging in challenging conversations and receiving feedback. Demonstrates persistence when outreach efforts do not immediately result in engagement, maintains professionalism through rejection, and adapts approaches based on feedback or changing priorities. Technology and Data Management: Experience using Google Workspace and Asana, or similar platforms. Ability to quickly learn Salesforce and maintain accurate, detailed records. Comfortable learning new technologies, including AI-enabled productivity tools, to improve efficiency while maintaining data quality. Organization and Time Management: Effectively prioritizes and manages multiple responsibilities and competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Maintains organized systems for tracking outreach, data, and communications. Research and Strategic Thinking: Demonstrates strong research and critical thinking skills, including the ability to locate credible hard-to-find information, evaluate sources, synthesize findings, keep up with changes in the food industry, and use research to support the strategic decisions of the Sr. Corporate Relations Manager, US. Understanding of organizational strategy and policies, with the ability to recognize how individual tasks contribute to broader team and organizational goals. Global Perspective: Approaches work with an understanding of the global nature of the organization’s programs. Demonstrated awareness of global factors and their relevance to specific projects and responsibilities. Financial Acumen: Supports routine budget-related tasks such as tracking expenses and maintaining accurate records. Hiring Timeline Details Once your application has been reviewed, you will be notified via email with further details on the status of your application. If a candidate is moved forward, the interview process will be as follows: Work Simulation Exercise (completed remotely) Interview (via video call) For full details of our recruitment process please review this document . Compensation and Benefits The annual compensation range for this role is: $63,166 - $77,203 for candidates in based in the United States. $63,738 - $77,662 for candidates based in Canada At The Humane League, we believe in maintaining a fair and nondiscriminatory work environment. As part of our commitment to transparency, we have implemented a job architecture framework, which levels all of our roles according to size and complexity, as well as a compensation step system, which allows us to determine fair salaries for all. We also look at market data for each country that we operate in, to allow us to create specific salary bands per country. This work is time consuming and involves a cost to THL. Therefore, when expanding into a country for the first time, we only undertake this work towards the end of the recruitment process, when we know where our ideal candidate is based. In addition, we have adopted a no negotiation policy for salaries. To determine a job's level, we carefully consider a variety of factors, including a job's size and complexity, required experience, knowledge, and/or skills, internal comparability, and market data. Candidates whose experience places them at step 5 or above of their job level within our compensation structure will be awarded a “Senior” title designation. These practices are aligned with our organizational values and will help us ensure we maintain clear, consistent, and transparent HR processes. THL offers a unique and competitive benefits package. Each country will be provided with benefits that are applicable and relative to the location they are in. Therefore, your exact benefits package will be shared with you at the time of offer. However, as an idea, some of the benefits that are currently offered to our global team are: Unlimited paid time off The last Friday of every month off as a THL ‘Public Holiday’ called ‘Mend Your Heart Friday’ Enhanced sick pay Generous bereavement leave Generous personal emergency leave Sabbatical leave Enhanced parental leave Health insurance Life insurance Retirement contributions Internet allowance For candidates outside the United States, The Humane League will not be your direct employer. title: Zapiet: Head of Marketing
description: Headquarters: UK URL: https://zapiet.com/ Location: Remote, with a preference for candidates based in the UK Salary: £40,000–£50,000 per year, depending on experience Bonus: Performance-related bonus Reporting to: Chief Marketing Officer and Chief Executive Officer This is a remote role, and we welcome applications from suitably qualified candidates in other locations. However, candidates based in the UK are preferred due to working hours and the need to collaborate closely with Zapiet’s leadership team. About Zapiet Zapiet helps Shopify merchants offer exceptional pickup, delivery and shipping experiences. Our products are used by more than 10,000 merchants around the world, from independent businesses to some of the world’s best-known brands. We are a remote, bootstrapped SaaS company with ambitious plans for the next stage of our growth. We are looking for a commercially focused Head of Marketing to help more merchants discover, adopt and succeed with Zapiet’s products. The role As Head of Marketing, your primary responsibility will be to increase revenue by driving awareness, adoption and continued use of Zapiet’s products. You will turn our wider company and marketing strategy into focused campaigns that generate measurable results. You will own the marketing funnel, from discovery and acquisition through to activation, expansion and retention. You will also manage and grow a team of internal and external specialists across email marketing, SEO, answer engine optimisation, content, communications and other marketing disciplines. This is a hands-on leadership role. You should be comfortable setting strategy, managing specialists, analysing performance and stepping in to help execute when needed. You will work closely with our CMO, CEO, product, sales, partnerships and customer support teams. Your responsibilities Increase product adoption and revenue Develop and deliver marketing plans that increase installations, product adoption and recurring revenue. Identify the biggest opportunities within our acquisition, activation, retention and expansion funnels. Create campaigns that clearly communicate how Zapiet’s products help merchants increase revenue, reduce costs and improve their operations. Increase adoption across Zapiet’s complete product portfolio through cross-selling, product education and lifecycle marketing. Support new product and feature launches with clear positioning, messaging and go-to-market plans. Develop campaigns for specific industries, merchant segments and geographic markets. Turn merchant success stories into compelling case studies, campaigns and sales materials. Own marketing performance Set clear targets and KPIs for every marketing channel. Build reporting that connects marketing activity to installations, qualified opportunities, product adoption and recurring revenue. Monitor performance across the full funnel and identify where merchants are dropping off. Run structured experiments to improve conversion, activation and retention. Manage the marketing budget and allocate resources to the channels producing the strongest commercial results. Report performance, insights and priorities directly to the CMO and CEO. Lead and grow the marketing team Manage and develop a team of specialists across email marketing, SEO, AEO, content and communications. Recruit additional expertise as the marketing function grows. Set clear goals, responsibilities and performance expectations. Create an environment where specialists can do their best work while remaining accountable for measurable outcomes. Coordinate internal team members, agencies, freelancers and technology partners. Ensure campaigns are delivered on time and to a consistently high standard. Strengthen Zapiet’s market position Refine the positioning and messaging of Zapiet and its products. Improve Zapiet’s visibility across search engines, AI answer platforms, industry publications and the wider Shopify ecosystem. Build relationships with Shopify agencies, technology partners, influencers and ecommerce communities. Identify emerging changes in SaaS marketing, ecommerce discovery and merchant buying behaviour. Ensure Zapiet’s communications are clear, distinctive and consistent across every channel. What we are looking for Significant experience marketing SaaS products, ideally within ecommerce, Shopify or B2B software. A proven record of increasing product adoption, recurring revenue or qualified pipeline through marketing. Experience leading and developing a multidisciplinary marketing team. Strong knowledge of lifecycle and email marketing, SEO, content, communications and product marketing. A practical understanding of answer engine optimisation and how AI is changing product discovery. Experience developing and executing go-to-market plans for products and features. Strong analytical skills and the ability to connect marketing activity with commercial results. Experience setting targets, managing budgets and reporting performance to senior leadership. Excellent project management skills and the ability to keep multiple campaigns moving. Native-level written and spoken English, with exceptional attention to detail. A willingness to be hands-on and take ownership of outcomes. You will do well in this role if you Think about revenue and product adoption, not vanity metrics. Can turn a broad strategy into a focused and achievable plan. Understand how acquisition, activation, retention and expansion work together. Are comfortable challenging assumptions and testing new ideas. Know how to lead experts without needing to be the deepest specialist in every discipline. Communicate openly, make decisions using evidence and take responsibility for results. Enjoy working in a fast-moving, international and remote environment. How success will be measured Your performance will be assessed against agreed commercial and marketing targets, which may include: Growth in marketing-attributed recurring revenue. Growth in product installations and qualified merchant opportunities. Improvements in trial-to-paid and install-to-activation conversion. Increased adoption of additional Zapiet products. Growth in organic, email, partner and AI-assisted discovery channels. Merchant retention and expansion revenue. The performance and development of the marketing team. Efficient use of the marketing budget. A performance-related bonus will be paid based on the achievement of agreed targets. What we offer A salary of £40,000–£50,000 per year, depending on experience. A performance-related bonus. Remote and flexible working. The opportunity to shape the marketing strategy of an established, international SaaS company. Direct access to Zapiet’s CMO and CEO. The freedom to build a talented marketing team and introduce new ideas. The opportunity to work with Shopify merchants, agencies and technology partners around the world. Equal opportunities Zapiet welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. We make hiring decisions based on experience, ability and the contribution each person can make to our team. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/zapiet-head-of-marketing

title: Head of Trading & Brokerage
description: About the Company We are seeking an experienced and visionary Head of Market Making to establish and lead our Market Making and Liquidity Providing function. This is a strategic leadership role responsible for the end-to-end design, implementation, and management of a new Market Making desk, initially focusing on the Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) with a long-term vision to expand into GCC capital markets. About the Role The successful candidate will combine strategic leadership with hands-on trading expertise, driving liquidity, optimizing capital deployment, managing market risk, and generating sustainable revenue through efficient market making strategies. Responsibilities Design, establish, and lead the organization's Market Making and Liquidity Providing desk. Develop and execute market making strategies across listed securities. Build liquidity provision capabilities for the Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) and support future regional expansion. description: Nymbus (https://nymbus.com/) isn't just a leader in fintech; we're a community of innovators passionate about reimagining banking. Our award-winning modern core platform and cloud-based technology serve as the backbone for financial institutions eager to modernize and excel. We operate with an AI-first mindset across our business, continuously improving how we work and the value we deliver to our clients. Our culture is grounded in collaboration, accountability, and a strong commitment to execution. WORK ENVIRONMENT: Nymbus is a remote-first company. Occasional travel may be required for client engagements, team planning sessions, or project activities. Working hours primarily align with the Eastern Time Zone; candidates located in the Eastern or Central time zones are preferred. While standard business hours are expected, occasional after-hours support may be required for critical operational activities. POSITION SUMMARY: The Enterprise IT Support Specialist provides day-to-day technical and operational support for Enterprise IT. This role is responsible for onboarding and offboarding employees, identity and access management, endpoint administration, and supporting the technologies employees rely on every day. This is more than a traditional Help Desk role. We're looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, improving processes, and leveraging AI and automation to make Enterprise IT more efficient. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES: Provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 technical support for employees across hardware, software, SaaS applications, and collaboration tools. Administer identity and access management, including SSO, MFA, user accounts, and permissions. Configure, deploy, and support macOS and Windows devices using Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms. Document, prioritize, and resolve support requests using the IT Service Management (ITSM) platform. Maintain IT assets, software licensing, and operational documentation. Experience with cloud-based SaaS applications and ITSM platforms. Strong troubleshooting, communication, organization, and customer service skills. Self-starter with strong ownership, curiosity, and a continuous improvement mindset. Preferred Qualifications Experience with JumpCloud, Google Workspace, Jamf, or similar platforms. Experience with Jira Service Management. Familiarity with PowerShell, Bash, Python, or other automation tools. AI-First Expectations AI is transforming Enterprise IT, and we expect every member of our team to embrace it as part of how they work. Successful candidates will: Think AI first before approaching repetitive or manual work. Use AI to improve productivity, documentation, troubleshooting, and communication. Identify opportunities to automate routine tasks and improve operational efficiency. Continuously learn and apply new AI capabilities responsibly and securely. title: Data Analyst Assistant
description: We are adding a Data Analyst Assistant to the team to support a large scale engagement with an established Italian infrastructure group. This position focuses on interrogating financial assumptions and identifying discrepancies in complex portfolios to ensure our partner makes decisions based on hard evidence rather than corporate narratives. About Blue Oak Consulting Blue Oak Consulting provides independent advisory on pricing, portfolio economics, capital allocation, and acquisition assumptions. We are not a traditional consulting firm focused on broad transformation programs or high level strategy decks. Instead, we interrogate specific commercial decisions where the financial stakes are high and the existing narrative is not sufficient. Our team looks past corporate language and P&L complexity to identify where value is leaking or capital is trapped. We work across sectors like software, manufacturing, and healthcare to test whether the assumptions behind a growth plan or an acquisition actually hold under pressure. We are a small, principal led firm where the people who do the work are the ones accountable for the results. We do not take transaction contingent fees, which allows us to be completely honest about whether the economics of a decision make sense. Our goal is to provide clarity through financial discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism. The Role This is a full time, permanent position that is conducted entirely in a remote environment. You will work closely with our principals to dig into the numbers provided by our partners, often starting with the Italian infrastructure project. The goal is to move past P&L complexity and find where value might be leaking. You will be expected to think critically and ask why certain numbers exist high up in a spreadsheet, rather than just accepting them as facts. This role offers an attractive and competitive compensation package for an entry level professional looking to gain deep experience in financial analysis. What You Will Be Doing Cleaning and organizing large datasets from various sources to build a clear financial picture. Testing the logic behind pricing assumptions to see if they survive real world friction. Helping build financial models that track capital allocation across different infrastructure assets. Identifying outliers and anomalies in expenditure reports that do not align with the stated narrative. Updating portfolio economics trackers to reflect new acquisition data. Collaborating with the team through virtual channels to clarify findings and refine analysis. Preparing clear summaries of data trends that highlight potential financial risks. Verifying the accuracy of inputs used in growth forecasts for specific business units. Assisting in the interrogation of acquisition assumptions for new investment opportunities. What You Bring A degree or background in finance, economics, mathematics, or a related field with a heavy emphasis on data. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the ability to manage complex formulas and large tables. A skeptical mindset that enjoys finding inconsistencies in spreadsheets and reports. Comfort working in a fully remote setting where communication is largely written and specific. Ability to organize messy data into structured formats without losing important context. Interest in how large businesses actually spend money and allocate internal capital. Reliability and a willingness to learn how to scrutinize financial statements at a deep level. Strong attention to detail, especially when reviewing line items that seem out of place. What We Offer A fully remote work schedule that provides flexibility and removes the need for a daily commute. Direct access to firm principals who provide mentorship and clear feedback on your work. The opportunity to work on high stakes projects, such as our current work with the Italian infrastructure group. A professional environment focused on logic and evidence rather than corporate politics. Practical training in financial modeling and capital allocation analysis. A permanent, stable role within a firm that values individual accountability and results. At Blue Oak Consulting, we believe that clarity comes from discipline and a healthy amount of skepticism. We stay through the execution phase of our projects because we know that decisions looking sound in theory often face challenges once they meet reality. This role is a starting point for someone who wants to understand the mechanics of how value is created and protected in large organizations. We value the work over the performance, and we look for assistants who are eager to show how the numbers actually add up without relying on corporate jargon. title: Front End Developer
description: Career Opportunity Here's the corporate dribble HR made us put at the top: Acro Commerce is looking for a Front End Developer to build and maintain high-quality e-commerce experiences for our clients. That's done. Now here's what we really want. Someone who codes in React like it's their native tongue, but still talks to our crew comfortably and sometimes even the odd client. You can turn a Figma file into a fast, componentized, pixel-perfect build, and you notice when something's a few pixels off before anyone has to tell you. You're driven to do good work but don't take yourself too seriously while doing it. You also know your own code. You can walk us through a build that didn't go the way you planned, what you'd do differently, and you don't need your hand held to get there. That kind of honesty and low ego is how you got good in the first place. You must be able to provide example work. What You'll Do Build & Ship Build and maintain front ends primarily in React, Next.js, and TypeScript, turning Figma designs into clean, componentized, well-tested code Implement updates and revisions to existing websites and web applications Work independently across multiple smaller tasks or larger builds with shifting priorities to meet deadlines Quality & Estimation Produce high-quality work adhering to Acro Media standards and the Acro Media production process Provide accurate estimates for the time required to fix a defect, complete a build, or add functionality to an existing application Find and fix problems in code; this might not be your code, and your only hint might be a cryptic complaint from a client Collaboration Communicate well with Account Managers, Supervisors, and Clients about work requests, problems, and defects Act as both a peer/mentor to other developers and be comfortable asking for help from teammates What You'll Bring We're less concerned with degrees and more with what you can actually build. Formal education or prior experience is not required; we just want to know you can code, so you'll need to show us some work. Strong, hands-on React experience, comfortable building component-driven UIs and working from a design system or component library (Storybook experience a plus) An eye for design. You don't need to be a designer, but you should be able to look at a build next to a Figma file and know when something's off: spacing, type, hierarchy, polish, and ideally propose the fix Solid grasp of responsive, accessible front-end development; you build things that hold up across devices and know your WCAG basics without being asked We like frameworks, but show us what you can do without one; comfortable hand-coding clean HTML, CSS, and JS when the situation calls for it Comfortable working in a Linux shell for day-to-day tasks; some understanding of Linux hosting is a plus Source control experience (Git, GitHub, etc.) We're open to good programmers who know other languages and technologies and are willing to learn. Here's a bunch of stuff we normally work with: React, Next.js, and TypeScript are the core of this role, and the rest are a strong plus: JavaScript, Tailwind, SASS/SCSS, Figma, Drupal, Shopify, WordPress, Docker, Lando. Nice-to-haves beyond that include testing tools (Cypress, React Testing Library), other frontend frameworks (Bootstrap, MUI), package managers (npm, Yarn), CI tooling (Gulp, Grunt), and analytics/performance tools (Lighthouse, Google Analytics). If you're a badass Lisp hacker type, mention that too, and if you're creative outside of code (drawing, painting, music, whatever), we'd love to hear about that too. An excellent internet connection and adequate hardware are required; you must be able to sustain an hour-long conference call without any issues Fluency in English All offers of employment with Acro Commerce are contingent on successfully completing a criminal background check. Working remotely Given the often isolated nature of working remotely, we value remote team members who get involved, communicate effectively over email, chat, and video, and aren't afraid to show their face on a webcam. We want you to be part of the team, not just a fly on the wall. What We Bring Ownership and impact. Developers own this joint here. We're not going to stick you in a corner with headphones on and call you "the IT department." The expected salary range for this role for candidates residing in Canada is $50,000â$134,000 CAD, tailored to your skills, performance, qualifications, experience, and location. Autonomy over your schedule. Flex start times, earned days off, and real remote work. Prefer to start at 8:00? 9:00? We'll work with you. Want every second Friday off? We've got a program for that. Work from your home office or from our Kelowna HQ, your call. (Some client contracts require staff to be located in Canada, so most positions need you to be legally able to work here.) Professional development. We might live and breathe software development, but we are also really passionate about our team's personal development, too. We love to learn and are always striving to be the best version of ourselves; whether it's training on the latest technology or learning how to become a better delegator, we will help you improve your skills and hit your goals. Culture. We're a certain type of people. We're all a little different and unique in our own way, but we seem to work well together. No one's perfect, and we embrace that. We take our work seriously, but we don't take ourselves too seriously. Check out our site to get to know us! Feel free to dissect what and how we do what we do. All careers come with a 30-day no-questions-asked money-back guarantee. If you are in any way unsatisfied with your career, we will return you to the workforce at absolutely NO COST to you (minus shipping and handling). title: Junior Front End Developer
description: About PULSE (MENA) PULSE (MENA) is a forward-thinking organization committed to building innovative digital solutions that empower businesses and communities across the Middle East and North Africa. We are passionate about creating intuitive, accessible, and high-performing web applications that deliver exceptional user experiences. As we continue to expand, we are seeking a motivated Junior Front-End Developer who is eager to learn, collaborate, and grow within a remote-first team. Position Overview The Junior Front-End Developer will support the design, development, and maintenance of modern web applications and user interfaces. Working alongside experienced developers, designers, and product teams, you will contribute to building responsive, accessible, and visually engaging digital experiences while developing your technical expertise. This role is ideal for early-career developers, recent graduates, or individuals with internship, freelance, or personal project experience who are looking to launch their careers in front-end development. Key Responsibilities Front-End Development Develop responsive, mobile-friendly web pages using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. Assist in building reusable UI components and interactive user interfaces. Convert UI/UX designs into clean, functional, and responsive web applications. Ensure websites and applications are optimized for speed, performance, and usability. Test and maintain compatibility across modern browsers and devices. Application Maintenance Debug and resolve front-end issues and performance bottlenecks. Maintain and enhance existing web applications. Assist in implementing new features and improving user experience. Perform routine code updates and maintenance tasks. Collaboration Work closely with UI/UX designers, back-end developers, and product managers. Participate in Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives. Contribute to code reviews and team discussions. Communicate progress, challenges, and technical solutions effectively. Code Quality Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code. Follow coding standards, development best practices, and version control procedures. Participate in testing, quality assurance, and bug-fixing activities. Continuously improve coding skills through mentorship and feedback. Continuous Learning Stay current with emerging front-end technologies and industry trends. Learn new frameworks, tools, and development methodologies. Participate in technical training and knowledge-sharing sessions. Contribute ideas that improve product quality and development efficiency. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). 0â2 years of experience in front-end development or web development. Internship, freelance, academic, or personal project experience is encouraged. Basic understanding of responsive web design principles. Familiarity with Git version control. Required Technical Skills Proficiency in HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+). Basic experience with React.js, Vue.js, or Angular. Understanding of responsive CSS frameworks such as Bootstrap or Tailwind CSS. Familiarity with REST APIs and JSON. Basic understanding of browser developer tools and debugging techniques. Knowledge of responsive design, web accessibility, and cross-browser compatibility. Preferred Qualifications Experience developing personal, academic, or portfolio web projects. Familiarity with TypeScript. Basic knowledge of state management libraries (Redux, Context API, Pinia, etc.). Experience working with Figma or other design collaboration tools. Familiarity with Vite, Webpack, npm, or Yarn. Exposure to Agile or Scrum development methodologies. Required Skills Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Excellent attention to detail. Effective verbal and written communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment. Strong organizational and time management skills. Adaptability and willingness to learn new technologies. Positive attitude and growth mindset. Technical Requirements Candidates Must Have Reliable high-speed internet connection. Personal laptop or desktop capable of running modern development tools. Quiet and professional home workspace. Webcam and headset for virtual meetings and team collaboration. Ability to install and use required development software and collaboration platforms. Working Hours Full-time remote position. Flexible working hours based on project and team requirements. Availability to collaborate across MENA time zones. Occasional participation in virtual meetings outside standard working hours when required. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Success In This Role Will Be Measured By Quality and maintainability of code. Timely completion of assigned development tasks. Bug resolution efficiency. Compliance with coding standards and best practices. Team collaboration and communication. Continuous learning and professional development. Contribution to successful project delivery. What We Offer Fully remote work environment. Competitive salary. Structured onboarding and mentorship. Continuous learning and professional development opportunities. Career advancement within PULSE (MENA). Collaborative, innovative, and inclusive work culture. Exposure to modern technologies and exciting digital projects. Performance-based recognition and growth opportunities. Core Competencies We Are Looking For Individuals Who Demonstrate Passion for technology and innovation. Accountability and professionalism. Strong attention to detail. Initiative and continuous learning. Team collaboration. Adaptability and resilience. Problem-solving ability. Creativity and curiosity. Effective communication. Commitment to delivering high-quality work. Equal Opportunity Employer PULSE (MENA) is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where all employees are valued and respected. We welcome applications from qualified candidates regardless of gender, nationality, age, disability, religion, or background. How to Apply If you are passionate about front-end development, eager to grow your technical skills, and excited to contribute to innovative digital products in a remote-first environment, we encourage you to apply. Join PULSE (MENA) and help create modern, user-focused digital experiences that make a lasting impact across the MENA region. title: garden3d: Head of Design
description: Headquarters: New York City URL: https://garden3d.net/ We are hiring a Head of Design for the garden3d creative collective, to uphold an exceedingly high bar on every single thing we make More details if you check our original job posting link About garden3d We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions. Our client roster includes Google , Stripe , Figma , Hinge , Black Socialists in America , ACLU , Pratt , Parsons , Mozilla , The Nobel Prize , MIT , Gnosis , Etsy & Gagosian . We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill , and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space . We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs. Sanctuary Computer — Development At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson. Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development. XXIX — Design When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be. We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility. Index Space — Community A network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools. We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care. garden3d TK — Media At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture. We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music. Plus, our partner organizations https://www.thelightphone.com/ https://www.mill.com/ https://www.ingredient-ai.com/ The Head of Design Role The garden3d Head of Design has one mandate: nothing we put on the internet falls below an 8 out of 10. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and all of them ship work into the world under our name. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis , this person sets the craft standard, and builds the culture that holds it. You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you. This role works with studio leads, designers, developers, editors, animators, photographers and clients across every garden3d vertical. This person can move between a brand identity, a product interface, a case study and a launch film in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them. They span all of garden3d, but their home base is XXIX . Our design studio is where the standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips, so this person runs critique there. Regular reviews. Honest and specific feedback. A shared language for why one thing is better than another, and what practically to do about it. Then they carry that same bar everywhere: to Sanctuary Computer's product and web work, to Index, to new USB Club product launches, to garden3d TK and everything we publish. They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the designers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Figma and The Nobel Prize, and sees a design practice they can propel among the best in the world. Responsibilities & Mandates ‍Quality never less than 8/10 We aspire for 10/10, celebrate 9/10 and never publish anything that’s not an 8/10 - visually, narratively, and in production quality. This person holds that line across every website, brand, deck, film, case study and post, on every vertical. They would rather kill a piece than let a 6 out the door. Their feedback makes work better and faster, without micromanaging the people who make it. A critique culture at XXIX XXIX is where our standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They build and run its critique practice: reviews with teeth, feedback that is specific rather than polite, and a vocabulary the whole studio shares. A designer should leave a crit knowing exactly what to do next. Done well, the crit is what makes the studio better than any one person in it, including them. Hiring and empowering the very best They are a magnet for exceptional designers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so. Client craft, at blue-chip standard Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize and Gagosian. This person has sat across the table from companies like these, presented work, defended it, and shaped a brand narrative the client's own leadership could repeat back to their board. They can run a room, and they've done it across many industries, not just one. New design business, and the projects that matter most They run new business for design. Pitching, scoping and closing the work we actually want, and building the relationships that bring the next one back. When a project is our highest-profile or highest-budget, they're in it: not always as the day-to-day lead, but as the person shaping the creative direction and making sure it lands. The work we win, and the work we're known for, is the clearest measure of whether this is going well. Type and editorial design Typography and editorial systems are core craft here, not a specialism we farm out. This person has a real practice in both. Their type choices should be one of the first things you notice about their portfolio, and one of the first things our designers learn from them.
